title: Presentation: Architecting the Data Layer for AI Agents: From Transactional Systems to MCP and Semantic Models
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/enterprise-data-architecture-ai-agents/en/mediumimage/fabiane-nardon-medium-1787218382028.jpeg"/><p>Fabiane Nardon shares how TOTVS prepares enterprise data for token-hungry AI agents. She discusses balancing deterministic logic and non-deterministic LLMs across precision, security, and cost. Nardon details using data mesh, low-latency database architectures, semantic ontologies, and dynamic MCP tool selection to optimize context windows and reduce token overhead in transactional systems.</p> <i>By Fabiane Nardon</i>

title: Cloudflare Workers Accept Inbound TCP, with gRPC the First Protocol on Top
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/workers-inbound-tcp-grpc/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787654507205.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare Workers can now accept inbound TCP connections through a new connect(socket) handler routed via Spectrum, ending an eight-year restriction to HTTP. Containers get full-duplex gRPC in any language, while Workers get unary and server-streaming through automatic gRPC-web translation. Everything is private beta.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: FreeToken Unlocks Frontier MoE Inference on Consumer Hardware via Dynamic Co-Execution
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Researchers from UC Berkeley and MIT have developed FreeToken, an open-source inference engine that enhances the utility of Mixture-of-Experts models on consumer hardware. By implementing a dynamic scheduling policy and optimising weight management, FreeToken improves decoding speeds and execution efficiency in edge AI applications, fostering self-hosted reasoning systems.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Uber Builds GitFarm to Run Git Operations as a Service for Large-Scale Monorepos
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Uber’s GitFarm provides Git operations as a centralized service, eliminating local repository clones across large scale monorepo workloads. The platform uses prewarmed checkouts, ephemeral sandboxes, repository synchronization, and gRPC streaming to reduce resource consumption and startup latency for automation services operating across thousands of repositories.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: AKS Looks to Make Node Disruption More Predictable with New NAP Guidance
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/aks-node-disruption/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787153940553.jpg"/><p>Microsoft is placing greater emphasis on controlling disruption in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) Node Auto-Provisioning (NAP), publishing new guidance to help platform teams balance the efficiency benefits of automated node consolidation with application availability.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: From DVDs to Global Streaming: How Netflix’s Commerce Architecture Actually Evolved
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/netflix-commerce-architecture-evolution/en/mediumimage/kasia-trapszo-medium-1787217920531.jpg"/><p>Kasia Trapszo discusses how Netflix evolved its commerce platform from a U.S. DVD service into global infrastructure. She explains navigating international payment realities, adapting to strict regulatory mandates, decomposing monolithic architectures along domain boundaries, and re-architecting systems for massive live-event demand - proving great systems survive by continually evolving.</p> <i>By Kasia Trapszo</i>

title: Article: Post-Quantum Cryptography in Spring Boot: Four Patterns You Can Ship This Sprint
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/pqc-in-spring-boot/en/headerimage/pqc-in-spring-boot-header-1787646727709.jpg"/><p>There are four patterns that bring PQC into a Spring Boot fleet: encrypting payloads between services, locking down database fields, signing documents that need to hold up for decades, and moving service tokens off RS256. Along the way, we discuss why Harvest Now, Decrypt Later is already happening, and why none of this is production-safe until KMS or Vault is in place.</p> <i>By Pankaj Sharma</i>

title: Meta Expands Its Custom Silicon Strategy From Compute Into Networking
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>Meta has detailed MTIA 300, its first in-house accelerator optimized for training ranking and recommendation models.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

title: Audio Fingerprinting Discovered on Alibaba Websites While Debugging BLE Multipoint Disconnects
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>A recent discovery revealed that AliExpress employs silent audio streams for device fingerprinting, leveraging the Web Audio API. This technique involves analyzing hardware-specific audio processing to distinguish user devices. Privacy-focused browsers have developed countermeasures, highlighting a security gap in current web standards regarding audio context initialization and user privacy.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Spring News Roundup: First Milestone Releases for Boot, Framework, Data, Security, Modulith, Batch
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/spring-news-roundup-aug17-2026/en/headerimage/spring-news-roundup-image-1787845727439.jpg"/><p>After a 10-week hiatus since the last batch of Spring ecosystem releases, there was a flurry of activity during the week of August 17th, 2026, highlighting first milestone releases of: Spring Boot, Spring Framework, Spring Data, Spring Security, Spring Integration, Spring HATEOAS, Spring Modulith, Spring Batch, Spring AMQP and Spring for Apache Kafka.</p> <i>By Michael Redlich</i>

title: Google Cloud Launches AI-powered Agents to Simplify Database Lifecycle Management
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/google-database-operation-agents/en/headerimage/google-database-operations-agents-1787842474177.jpeg"/><p>Google Cloud has introduced AI-powered Database Operations Agents, featuring an Onboarding Agent that streamlines database setup and an Observability Agent that helps automate troubleshooting, performance optimization, and tuning. Integrated with Gemini Cloud Assist, these agents support multiple database services, including AlloyDB, Bigtable, and Spanner.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Astro Introduces Sätteri: A Rust-powered Markdown And Mdx Processor With Up To 60% Faster Builds
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/astro-satteri-rust/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787817978309.jpg"/><p>Sätteri is a high-performance Markdown and MDX processor developed by the Astro team. Built in Rust, it enhances build speeds by up to 61% for Astro 7.0. Sätteri supports flexible JavaScript plugins and integrates various Markdown features natively. It maintains compatibility with the unified ecosystem while offering faster parsing and reduced dependencies.</p> <i>By Daniel Curtis</i>

title: How to Make Testing More Sustainable
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/making-testing-sustainable/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787339384932.jpg"/><p>By using a sustainable testing strategy, you can skip unnecessary tests, ensure failing fast and early, and only run tests affected by code changes. Tracking energy use per test and using static code analysis can help spot inefficiencies and guide optimization efforts.</p> <i>By Ben Linders</i>

title: Presentation: Python, Numba, and Algorithm Design: Building Efficient Models in Financial Services
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/numba/en/mediumimage/chad-schuster-medium-1787217755995.jpeg"/><p>Chad Schuster discusses bridging Python's developer velocity with C-like performance using Numba JIT and GPUs. Drawing from large-scale actuarial modeling, he explains LLVM pipeline architecture, performance gains up to 750x, and essential trade-offs like OOP limits, type inference errors, and compile-time overhead for engineering leaders scaling compute-heavy enterprise systems.</p> <i>By Chad Schuster</i>

title: Cloudflare Wallets Arrives Late to x402, and the Spending Controls Stop at the Payment
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/08/agent-payment-rails-x402/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787649155466.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare announced Wallets, giving agents a stablecoin balance and spending controls, though only handle claiming is live and squatting complaints have already surfaced. Payments run on x402, now hosted by the Linux Foundation. The controls bound single payments, not sequences, leaving composition to the application above.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>
